summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports that the Uhud martyrs, exhumed about forty years later during Mu'aawiya's canal digging, were still fresh, including his father Abdullaah bin Amr and Amr bin Jamooh who shared one grave.

people.name: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdullaah bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Sa'sa'a

notes: Several separate reports run together: Jaabir's accounts, the Ansaar scholars' report, and Abdur Rahmaan's report of the shared grave.

summary: Jaabir reports that when the canal was dug near the Uhud martyrs, a spade struck Hamzah's foot and it bled after forty years.
notes: Contains a second report of the same event ('Another narration') and the author's comment citing Sheikh Samhodi's Wafaa'ul Wafaa; Samhodi is a cited authority and is not tagged as a person.

summary: Muhammad bin Shurahbeel narrates that a Companion took sand from the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh, found it to be musk, and the Prophet exclaimed Subhaanallaah.
Another report says that someone took sand from the grave of Sa'd bin Mu'aadh and found it had become musk.
notes: The narrator is unnamed; this is a variant of n03603.

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri says that while digging Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's grave, the fragrance of musk rose with each shovelful of sand.
Urwa reports that after the Bir Ma'oonah massacre, Aamir bin Tufayl saw the martyr Aamir bin Fuhayrah lifted to the sky, and the Prophet told the Sahabah the martyrs were pleased with their Rabb.
notes: The second paragraph is a separate note on Urwa bin Asmaa and Mundhir bin Amr, after whom Urwa and Mundhir bin Zubayr were named. The narrator 'Urwa' is not identified; Amr bin Umayyah is matched to the Damri entry.

summary: Another report says that the man who killed Aamir bin Fuhayrah, Jabbaar bin Sulma, asked what success Aamir had meant and then accepted Islaam.
notes: Text says 'Jabbaar bin Sulma Kalbi'; matched to jabbaar-bin-salma-kilaabi.

summary: Urwa reports that because Aamir bin Fuhayrah's body could not be found, the Sahabah believed the angels had buried him.
notes: Narrator 'Urwa' is unidentified (see n03606).

summary: The Prophet says the angels buried Aamir bin Fuhayrah and his soul was taken to 'Illiyyeen, and Aamir bin Tufayl describes seeing that Sahabi lifted between earth and sky.
notes: Two reports: the Prophet's words, then a separate report of Aamir bin Tufayl's words. The 'lttiyyeen' spelling is OCR debris for 'Illiyyeen'.

summary: Amr bin Umayyah reports untying Khubayb's body from the cross and finding it gone into the earth, and Dahhaak reports the Prophet sending Miqdaad and Zubayr who found the body fresh and the ground then took it.
notes: Two reports: Amr bin Umayyah's account, then Dahhaak's account of the Prophet's dispatch. Tan'eem is a place and the Mushrikeen are unnamed.

summary: Anas and Abu Hurayrah report that the grave of Alaa bin Hadhrami was found empty after burial, filled with light, or could not be located again.
notes: Opens with an elided start ('The beginning of the narration has been quoted'), and includes a separate report from Abu Hurayrah. The author's references (Bidaayah, Abu Nu'aym, Bayhaqi) are not tagged.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that the Prophet sent Aasim bin Thaabit on an expedition, and Allaah protected his body from the Quraysh with a swarm of wasps.
notes: The Quraysh are unnamed.

summary: Urwa reports that when the Mushrikeen tried to cut off Aasim bin Thaabit's head, Allaah sent wasps that stung them and stopped them.
notes: Narrator 'Urwa' is unidentified (see n03606).

summary: Hamzah bin Abu Usayd reports that the Prophet, going to a funeral at Baqee, told a wolf blocking the path to take its share, and advised a fixed one goat per year from each flock of forty or more.
notes: Hamzah bin Abu Usayd is not in the approved list; the approved abu-usayd-saaidi is his father, so not used. The Ansaari whose funeral it was is unnamed.

summary: Mutallib bin Abdullaah reports a wolf coming to the Prophet in Madinah with a proposal for a share of the flocks, and a Juhaynah man reports a delegation of about a hundred wolves that the Prophet sent away.
notes: Two reports: Mutallib's account of the single wolf, then the Juhaynah man's account of the delegation. The Juhaynah man is unnamed.

summary: Safeenah, the Prophet's freed slave, reports that a lion guided him out of the forest after a shipwreck, and in another account the lion led him when he lost his way.
notes: Two accounts of the same lion incident, the second introduced with 'In another narration'.

summary: Ibn Munkadir reports that Safeenah, lost in Roman territory, met a lion that accepted his claim to be the Prophet's freed slave, then walked beside him and led him to the army.
notes: 'Ibn Munkadir' is matched to muhammad-bin-munkadir (not sahabi).

summary: Wahab bin Abaan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar moved a lion off the road, and then quoted the Prophet that whoever fears and hopes in none but Allaah will not be overpowered by anything else.
notes: Wahab bin Abaan is not in the approved list and his Companion status is not known.

summary: Auf bin Maalik reports that a lion in a church in Areeha told him that Mu'aawiya, son of Abu Sufyaan, would be among the people of Jannah.
Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that a wolf spoke to a shepherd about the Prophet, and the Prophet confirmed it; a similar wolf spoke to Abu Sufyaan and Safwaan bin Umayyah about the Prophet's call.
notes: Two incidents: the wolf and the shepherd who brought his goats to Madinah, then the wolf that spoke to Abu Sufyaan and Safwaan. The shepherd is unnamed.

summary: Qais bin Hajjaaj reports that Amr bin al-Aas refused the Egyptians' ritual of throwing a girl into the Nile, Umar's letter had a note cast into the river, and the Nile then rose.
notes: Qais bin Hajjaaj is not in the approved list; his teacher is unnamed.

summary: Urwa A'ma reports that Abu Rayhaana's needle fell into the sea and, after he prayed for it, surfaced in his hand.
notes: Urwa A'ma is a freed slave of Banu Sa'd; his Companion status is not known.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Alaa bin Hadhrami, sent by the Prophet to Bahrain, crossed the sea by reciting Bismillaah, brought rain after a prayer and du'aa, and that his grave was later found empty.
Abu Hurayrah adds that the Persian governor Ibn Muka'bir, on seeing the Muslims, said they could never be fought and sailed back to Persia.
notes: Continuation of Abu Hurayrah's account in n03623.

summary: Anas reports that Umar appointed Alaa bin Hadhrami to lead an army, and that Alaa's du'aa brought rain and a crossing of the gulf without the animals' hooves getting wet.
notes: Ends with 'The narration still continues further.'

summary: Several accounts describe Alaa bin Hadhrami's du'aa for rain, his crossing of the sea with his men at Daareen, and Abu Bakr's dispatch of him to fight the Murtaddeen in Bahrain.
notes: Several narrations are joined. Some quotations are cut off in the text, such as the du'aa and the 'Forge for us a path' quote.

summary: Ibn Rufayl reports that Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, unable to find boats, led the army across the Tigris after Aasim bin Amr and sixty men went ahead, and the Persians fled the town of Bahurseer.
notes: Ibn Rufayl is not in the approved list and is unidentified.

summary: Several narrators describe the Muslim army crossing the Tigris at Madaa'in: Sa'd and Salmaan were assured the waters were subject, the rising mounds were seen, and the Persians fled, calling them madmen.
notes: Many reports are joined (Abu Bakr bin Hafs, Abu Uthmaan Nahdi, Umayr Saa'idi, Qais, Habeeb bin Suhbaan). Narrators not in the approved list are unidentified. Hujr bin Adi and Qa'qaa bin Amr are the Companions named in the text; the Persians and the other Muslims are unnamed.

summary: A'mash reports that a Muslim plunged into the Tigris saying Bismillaah, his horse rode over the water, and the other Muslims followed, which made the Persians flee.
notes: The companion A'mash heard the account from is unnamed.

summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that Tameem Daari, when Umar sent him, pushed back a fire that came from Harra with his bare hands, and Umar said such a witness cannot be like one who has not seen it.
notes: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal, Musaylama's son-in-law, is not in the approved list; his Companion status is not clear.

summary: Mu'aawiya bin Harmal reports that after repenting of fighting for Musaylama, Umar sent him to Tameem Daari, who pushed a fire from Harra back through its door and came out unharmed.
notes: Same narrator as n03630; this is his own account of his repentance.

summary: Another narration has Umar telling Tameem Daari that they keep him hidden for emergencies like this, but the text breaks off.
notes: Cut off after 'O Abu'.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that during Isha, Hasan and Husayn climbed on the Prophet's back in sajdah, and a flash of lightning lit their way home; another account has Hasan walking home by lightning.
notes: Two narrations: Abu Hurayrah's account of both boys, then a second account about Hasan alone. Their mother is not named.

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that on a stormy night the Prophet saw Qataadah bin Nu'maan in lightning and gave him a date-palm branch that lit the way and was to be used against a Shaytaan.
notes: The opening sentence refers to the Jumu'ah hour, but the story that follows is about the Isha prayer.

summary: Qataadah bin Nu'maan says that the Prophet's branch lit his way home and he struck a hedgehog in his house, which he took for a Shaytaan.
Anas reports that two Companions leaving the Prophet at night had lights shine before them, and each kept a light until they reached home.
notes: The two Companions are unnamed here (see n03637).

summary: Anas reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr and another Ansaari, leaving the Prophet on a dark night, each had their staff light up, and the second report names the other man as Abbaad bin Bishr.
notes: Two reports of the same event; the second names the other companion as Abbaad bin Bishr.

summary: Hamzah bin Amr Aslami reports that his fingers shone on a dark night so the Companions could gather their mounts, and at Tabook his fingers gave light to recover the Prophet's fallen luggage.
notes: Two reports: the dark night, then Tabook when the Munaafiqeen made the Prophet's camel bolt. The Munaafiqeen are unnamed.

summary: Zaid bin Abu Abs reports that his father, Abu Abs, after praying behind the Prophet, had his staff light up on a dark rainy night so he could reach his locality.
notes: Zaid bin Abu Abs is not in the approved list. The parenthetical note that Abu Abs was at Badr is the author's.

summary: Another account says that the Prophet gave Abu Abs bin Jabr a staff when his eyesight became weak, and it lit up a wide area for him.
notes: Narrator is unnamed.
